items.body:
> **Written 2026-10-08** (Security & Authorization Domain Agent), from the Chief Architect analysis of #2617 (comment 6062021008) and the Security ruling on #2617 ("Security ruling (2026-10-08)"). It carries the work #2617 identified; #2617 itself is not implemented. **It BLOCKS S24 (#2517).**

> **Revised 2026-10-08** (Security & Authorization Domain Agent), from the Security confirmation on the ADR-0072 draft (louisburroughs/durion#571, https://github.com/louisburroughs/durion/pull/571#issuecomment-6062991022). Seven changes:
> - `scheme` and `region` shape checks (item 8; the "Decisions applied" row);
> - a new AC 20 for those checks;
> - the reveal reason check and the `REASON_REJECTED` outcome (items 9 and 10);
> - the W-9 refusal case in AC 11;
> - the `registrationNumber` suffix rule in the guard (item 13; AC 16);
> - the key-policy wording (item 4);
> - the shape count in the incident check (item 15).
>
> Nothing else changed. Status stays `status:ready-for-dev`.

Part of CAP:550 (louisburroughs/durion#550). Domain: security, with supplier and accounting. Repo: `louisburroughs/durion-positivity-backend`. Modules:
- `pos-domain-events`
- `pos-supplier`
- the permission row in `pos-security-service`, `pos-security-common` and `pos-api-gateway`
- `docs/OPERATIONS_RUNBOOK.md`

## Story Intent

**As a** controller responsible for vendor records, **I want**:
- the vendor fact and every copy of it to carry only a vendor's tax-registration scheme, region and last four characters;
- the full number held encrypted in pos-supplier, masked on every read, and shown only to a permitted person who gives a reason and is audited;

**so that** a sole proprietor's SSN or SIN, or any business number, never sits in clear on Kafka, in a DLQ, in an outbox replay, in a replica, in a log or in a backup.

## Ruling summary

The Security ruling on #2617 governs this story; the comment carries the full text. In short:
- **Every number is RESTRICTED** (ruling 1), whatever its scheme. A personal number filed under a business scheme cannot be detected, so classifying by scheme fails open.
- **The fact** carries `TaxRegistration(scheme, region, last4)` at `schemaVersion` 2, on the same `eventType` and topic. There is no `.v2` topic and no dual-publish (ruling 9; the ADR-0044 §3 amendment).
- **`last4`** (CONFIDENTIAL) is the last 4 alphanumerics after separators are removed, and `null` below 8 (ruling 2).
- **At rest:** AES-256-GCM with the `AuditPayloadCipher` envelope and fail-closed key policy, under a separate key, with AAD bound to tenant, vendor and registration (ruling 3).
- **Reads are masked.** The number is revealed only through `supplier:vendor_tax_id:reveal` (ADMIN, CONTROLLER), with a reason and an audit row written in the same transaction (ruling 4).
- **Personal-id schemes are accepted** (ruling 5). The closed scheme vocabulary is a later pos-tax stub and does not block this story.
- **Cleanup:** outbox scrub; an alpha broker and DLQ purge; an incident check that outputs counts only (ruling 6). The runbook prints DLQ metadata only (ruling 7). The contract test gains a name guard (ruling 8).

## Scope

### In scope
- **`pos-domain-events`:**
  - `SupplierVendorUpdatedV1.TaxRegistration` becomes `(scheme, region, last4)`, and `SCHEMA_VERSION` becomes 2;
  - the Javadoc's "What is never here" section gains the full registration number;
  - `DomainEventContractTest` gains the restricted-name guard.
- **`pos-supplier`:**
  - encrypted storage, `registrationId` and stored `last4`;
  - the backfill;
  - the outbox scrub;
  - the masked `VendorView`;
  - the keep-by-`registrationId` update rule;
  - the reveal endpoint, its audit table and the read of that table;
  - the publisher change;
  - the key configuration;
  - README.
- **Permissions:** `supplier:vendor_tax_id:reveal` (new bit). Grants go to ADMIN and CONTROLLER, and the SUPPORT seed comment is updated (ruling 4 confirms `supplier:vendor:read` for SUPPORT).
- **Docs:** the DLQ inspection procedure in `docs/OPERATIONS_RUNBOOK.md`.
- **Alpha operations:** the incident count, then the broker and DLQ purge after deploy.

### Out of scope (and where it lives)
- **S24 (#2517):** the copy in pos-accounting and the `schemaVersion >= 2` consumer rule. The Accounting Domain amends S24 from the ruling. This story only must merge first.
- **S36 (#2525) and pos-order's copy:** already at the ADR-0044 R3 minimum, so nothing changes.
- **#2615:** wording only. `payeeTinLast4` reads the copy's `last4`. Accounting's to change.
- **The closed, classified scheme vocabulary:** a pos-tax stub (AW48) that Accounting specifies, with pos-supplier validating against it. Ruling 5 makes it a later story. It does not block S24.
- **The data-classification ADR** and the ADR-0044 §3 / ADR-0070 Decision 7 amendments: the ADR Generator, as the platform owner decides. They are a **merge gate** for this story (see Dependencies).
- **The vendor pages** (S30, louisburroughs/durion-positivity-frontend#469): masked display and the reveal action. See "Frontend-visible".
- **Re-encrypting stored numbers under a newer key:** a later operation. Decrypt-only previous keys cover rotation now.

## Specification references
- **Security ruling:** #2617, "Security ruling (2026-10-08)", rulings 1-9.
- **Architect analysis:** #2617 comment 6062021008, §3 "Recommendation" and "Versioning and migration impact".
- **ADRs:**
  - ADR-0044: R3, §3 (as amended), §4;
  - ADR-0050 §7 (cipher);
  - ADR-0070 Decision 7 (as amended);
  - ADR-0062 (RLS);
  - ADR-0018 and ADR-0022 (actor);
  - ADR-0046 (logging).
- **Security decisions:** DECISION-INVENTORY-001, -002 and -013.
- **SPEC-accounting-workspace:** §4.9 "Vendors (AW23)", "The fact"; AW48.

## Existing code

Verified on `main` at `8e9262491`. `SUP` = `pos-supplier/src/main/java/com/positivity/supplier/internal/`.

1. **The fact.** `pos-domain-events/.../supplier/SupplierVendorUpdatedV1.java`:
   - `TaxRegistration(scheme, number, region)`, with `number` non-null;
   - `SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`;
   - the "What is never here" section lists bank details only.

   `SupplierVendorUpdatedV1Test#taxRegistrationsAreCopied` (l.73) asserts the number travels. `#carriesNoBankDetails` (l.110) is the negative-test precedent.
2. **The publisher.** `SUP/vendor/service/VendorFactPublisher.toFact` copies `scheme`, `number` and `region` verbatim. `publish` writes the envelope through `SupplierOutboxEventWriter`, with `schemaVersion = SupplierVendorUpdatedV1.SCHEMA_VERSION`.
3. **Storage.**
   - `SUP/entity/SupplierVendorEntity.java` l.66-69: `tax_registrations jsonb` of `VendorTaxRegistration(scheme, number, region)` (`SUP/entity/VendorTaxRegistration.java`), in clear.
   - Created in `V3__vendor_master.sql` l.39. V3's backfill from profiles writes `[]`.
   - The latest migration is V3.
4. **API.**
   - `SUP/vendor/service/model/TaxRegistrationDto.java` is used for input **and** output. `number` is required, up to 64 characters. `@Schema` example `123456789RT0001`.
   - `VendorView.taxRegistrations` is `List<TaxRegistrationDto>`, so `GET /v1/supplier/vendors` and `/{vendorId}` return full numbers to `supplier:vendor:read`.
   - `SupplierVendorServiceImpl` (`SUP/vendor/service/`):
     - `replaceTaxRegistrations` (l.433) replaces the whole list when it differs;
     - `toEntity` (l.440);
     - `toView` (l.474).
   - `SUP/controller/SupplierVendorController.java` l.74 has the example `{"scheme":"EIN","number":"12-3456789"}`. So does `pos-supplier/openapi.yaml` l.3741 and l.5983.
5. **Outbox.** `supplier_event_outbox` (`V1__baseline_supplier.sql` l.121): `event_type varchar(128)`, `payload text` (the whole `DomainEventEnvelope`, fact under `payload`, version under `schemaVersion`), `last_error text`.
   - No purge exists.
   - `SupplierOutboxReplayService.replayEventsBetween` re-queues stored rows verbatim (`supplier.outbox.replay-requested`).
   - `POST /v1/supplier/vendors/facts/replay` (`supplier:fact:replay`) re-emits current state.
6. **Cipher.** `SUP/entity/AuditPayloadCipher.java`:
   - AES-256-GCM, with envelope `version | keyIdLen | keyId | nonce | ciphertext+tag` and the header as AAD;
   - decrypt-only `previous-keys`;
   - a key required unless every active profile is `dev` or `test`;
   - bound from `SUPPLIER_AUDIT_ENC_KEY`.

   `AuditPayloadCipherTest` covers the key policy, including the empty and unrecognised profile cases.
7. **Permissions.**
   - `SUP/security/SupplierPermissions.java`: `supplier:vendor:read`, `:write`, `supplier:vendor_remit:approve` and `supplier:fact:replay` (bits 549-552).
   - `R__seed_role_permissions.sql` l.335-346 grants:
     - `vendor:read` to ADMIN, CONTROLLER, ACCOUNTING_CLERK, GENERAL_MANAGER and SUPPORT (SUPPORT marked "pending Security owner confirmation");
     - `supplier:audit:read` to ADMIN, SYSTEM_ADMINISTRATOR and SUPPORT.
   - There are three version-locked catalogs at `CATALOG_VERSION = 102`: `PermissionCode`, `GatewayPermissionCatalog` and `DownstreamPermissionCatalog`. Bit 558 is the highest in use. `RolePermissionBaselineTest#supportIsReadOnly` allows SUPPORT only `:view` and `:read`.
8. **Contract test.** `pos-domain-events/src/test/.../DomainEventContractTest.java` scans every event record (`scanRecords`, l.124). It has no field-name guard.
9. **Runbook.** `docs/OPERATIONS_RUNBOOK.md` l.1257-1261 inspects DLQs with `kafka-console-consumer.sh --from-beginning --max-messages 10`, which prints values.
10. **Consumers.** Five groups read `supplier.events.v1` and skip `supplier.vendor.updated` by `eventType`. None stores or reads a registration. No frontend code references `taxRegistrations` yet.

## Functional behaviour (PROPOSED)

### A. The fact (`pos-domain-events`, `pos-supplier`)

1. `SupplierVendorUpdatedV1.TaxRegistration(@NonNull String scheme, @Nullable String region, @Nullable String last4)`. The record name stays `...V1`, following the `ProductUpdatedV1` precedent.
   - `SCHEMA_VERSION = 2`. Its Javadoc cites the ADR-0044 §3 amendment (RESTRICTED withdrawal).
   - The record Javadoc's "What is never here" section adds: "A full tax-registration number. Registrations carry scheme, region and the last four characters only (Security ruling on #2617)."
2. `VendorFactPublisher.toFact` maps each stored registration to `(scheme, region, last4)` from the **stored** `last4`. It never decrypts.

### B. Storage (`pos-supplier`)

3. **Stored shape.** Each `tax_registrations` element becomes `{registrationId, scheme, region, last4, numberCiphertext}`:
   - `registrationId`: UUIDv7, stable for the life of the registration;
   - `last4`: computed at write by the ruling-2 rule;
   - `numberCiphertext`: base64 of the cipher envelope.

   No element has a `number` key. `VendorTaxRegistration` changes to match.
4. **Cipher.**
   - A vendor-tax-id cipher uses the same envelope and key policy as `AuditPayloadCipher`. Extracting the shared envelope and key-policy code is preferred to a copy.
   - Properties: `pos.supplier.vendor-tax-id.encryption.key`, `.key-id` (default `k1`) and `.previous-keys`. `application.yml` binds the key from `SUPPLIER_VENDOR_TAXID_ENC_KEY`.
   - The exchange-audit key is never used.
   - The AAD covers the envelope header **and** `tenantId`, `vendorId` and `registrationId`.
   - Startup fails without a key unless at least one profile is active and every active profile is `dev` or `test`. The failure message names `SUPPLIER_VENDOR_TAXID_ENC_KEY` and never prints key material.
   - Add the variable to the deployment env templates and to the secret store for alpha, as `SUPPLIER_AUDIT_ENC_KEY` is provisioned.
5. **Backfill.** Every existing clear number is encrypted, given a `registrationId` and given its `last4`.
   - SQL cannot hold the key, so this is a Flyway **Java** migration registered as a Spring bean (Spring Boot hands `JavaMigration` beans to Flyway), with the cipher injected. Version: next free pos-supplier version at merge (V4 or later today).
   - It is idempotent: an element with `numberCiphertext` and no `number` is left alone.
   - It honours RLS the way the module's existing migrations do: it binds each tenant, or runs as the RLS-exempt migration owner.
   - It logs counts only.
6. **Outbox scrub.** A Flyway SQL migration (the next free version at merge, after item 5's) rewrites every `supplier_event_outbox` row with `event_type = 'supplier.vendor.updated'`. Through `payload::jsonb`, and back to `text`:
   - each `payload.taxRegistrations[*]` loses `number` and gains `last4`, by the same rule: `regexp_replace(number, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g')`, its right 4 characters, or `null` under 8;
   - `schemaVersion` becomes 2;
   - `last_error` becomes `NULL`.

   Rows of every other event type are untouched. After the migration, no row of this type contains a `number` key.

### C. API (`pos-supplier`)

7. **Masked view.** A new `TaxRegistrationView(registrationId, scheme, region, last4)` replaces `TaxRegistrationDto` in `VendorView`. `GET` list and detail, create, update, deactivate, reactivate and remit-to responses all return it. No response carries `number`.
8. **Input.** `TaxRegistrationDto` becomes `(registrationId?, scheme, number?, region?)`:
   - **Has `registrationId`, no `number`:** keep the stored registration. `scheme` and `region` must equal the stored values; otherwise 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `fieldErrors[taxRegistrations[i].number]` "re-enter the number to change its scheme or region".
   - **Has `registrationId` and `number`:** replace that registration's number. The `registrationId` is kept, and `last4` and the ciphertext are recomputed.
   - **No `registrationId`:** a new registration. `number` is required (1-64 characters after trim).
   - **Unknown `registrationId`** for this vendor: 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`.
   - **Scheme and region shapes** (ADR-0072 Decision 2; Security confirmation on louisburroughs/durion#571). Every entry that carries a `number` is checked, so a stored attribute beside `last4` can never hold part of a number:
     - `scheme` is trimmed and upper-cased, then must match `^[A-Z][A-Z _/-]{0,15}$`: letters, spaces, `_`, `/` and `-`, at most 16 characters, no digit. It is stored upper-cased.
     - `region`, when present, is trimmed and upper-cased, then must match `^[A-Z]{2}(-[A-Z]{1,3})?$`: letters only, so `QC` and `CA-QC` pass and `US-123` does not. It is stored upper-cased.
     - Otherwise 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` with `fieldErrors[taxRegistrations[i].scheme]` or `fieldErrors[taxRegistrations[i].region]`. Neither the message nor the `fieldErrors` value nor any log line echoes the submitted value.
     - The closed vocabulary (#2623) later narrows `scheme` to listed codes. These shapes stay in force as a backstop.
   - **Omitted** stored registrations are removed.
   - **No-op detection** works on registration ids and stored values, never on ciphertext equality. A PUT that keeps every registration unchanged publishes nothing.
   - **No echo.** No error `message`, `fieldErrors` value, exception message or log line contains a submitted number.
   - **Fake examples.** `@Schema` and controller examples use obviously fake values: `"number": "000-00-0000"` for input; `"last4": "0000"` for output.
9. **Reveal.** `POST /v1/supplier/vendors/{vendorId}/tax-registrations/{registrationId}/reveal`, gated by `@PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('supplier:vendor_tax_id:reveal')")`. Body `{reason}`:
   - `reason` is trimmed, 10-500 characters; otherwise 400 `JUSTIFICATION_REQUIRED` (under 10) or `VALIDATION_ERROR` (over 500).
   - **The reason cannot carry the number.** This check runs after the 403 and 404 checks and after decryption.
     - Remove every non-alphanumeric character from both the reason and the stored number, then compare them case-insensitively.
     - If the reason contains the number: 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` with no echo. Nothing is revealed.
     - The refusal writes one audit row in the same transaction, with outcome `REASON_REJECTED` and `reason` null.
     - The reason is never logged, at any level.
   - An unknown vendor or registration answers 404 `SUPPLIER_VENDOR_NOT_FOUND` / `SUPPLIER_VENDOR_TAX_REGISTRATION_NOT_FOUND`.
   - **200** `{registrationId, scheme, region, number}`, with header `Cache-Control: no-store`.
   - In the **same transaction**, before the number is returned, insert one `supplier_vendor_tax_id_reveal` row. If the insert fails, the call fails and returns nothing.
   - A decryption failure answers 500 `SUPPLIER_VENDOR_TAX_ID_UNREADABLE`, is logged with vendorId, registrationId and key id only, and reveals nothing. The audit row still records the attempt.
   - A 403 writes nothing.
10. **Reveal audit read.** `GET /v1/supplier/vendors/{vendorId}/tax-id-reveals` (`supplier:audit:read`), paged with the module's existing list parameters (default 20, max 200), newest first.
    - Each row: `revealId`, `registrationId`, `scheme`, `revealedBy`, `revealedByRoles`, `reason`, `correlationId`, `revealedAt`, `outcome` (`REVEALED` | `UNREADABLE` | `REASON_REJECTED`).
    - `reason` is null on `REASON_REJECTED` rows only, and non-null on every other row.
    - Never the number or `last4`.
11. **Table.** `supplier_vendor_tax_id_reveal`, created in the same SQL migration as item 6 or its own, at the next free version:
    - tenant-scoped with RLS (ADR-0062);
    - append-only: no update or delete in code, and the application role has no `UPDATE` or `DELETE` grant if the module's convention allows it;
    - id UUIDv7.

    `revealedBy` comes from the security context (ADR-0018). `personId` is used if the module already stores it (ADR-0022).

### D. Permission

12. `supplier:vendor_tax_id:reveal`: `SupplierPermissions.VENDOR_TAX_ID_REVEAL`, with Javadoc citing the ruling.
    - Register it in `pos-supplier/src/main/resources/permissions.yaml`.
    - Bit: **the next free at merge** (559 is free on `main` today; S13 #2510 also takes the next free bit, so expect 560 or later). Write it through `scripts/generate-permissions.sh --sync --grant ADMIN --grant CONTROLLER` across all three catalogs, with the `CATALOG_VERSION` bump in all three. A bump means a fleet redeploy.
    - **Grants:** ADMIN and CONTROLLER in `R__seed_role_permissions.sql`, with a header bullet citing the ruling.
    - **No grant** to ACCOUNTING_CLERK, GENERAL_MANAGER, SUPPORT, SYSTEM_ADMINISTRATOR or any role in `role-permissions.csv`.
    - The SUPPORT `supplier:vendor:read` bullet (l.339-342) loses "Pending Security owner confirmation" and cites the ruling instead.

### E. Contract guard and runbook

13. `DomainEventContractTest` gains `noRestrictedFieldNames`, parameterized over the scanned records.
    - It walks record components recursively: nested records, `List`/`Set`/`Map` element types and arrays.
    - It fails on a name, compared case-insensitively, in: `number`, `ssn`, `sin`, `tin`, `itin`, `taxId`, `taxNumber`, `nationalId`, `accountNumber`, `routingNumber`, `iban`, `cardNumber`, `pan`, `cvv`, `password`, `secret`. It also fails on any name that ends with `registrationNumber`, compared case-insensitively (for example `supplierRegistrationNumber`), per ADR-0072 Decision 6 as confirmed on louisburroughs/durion#571.
    - A test-only record with a component `supplierRegistrationNumber` makes the guard fail.
    - A `Map<String, String> ALLOWED` in the test, with reason and sign-off per entry, holds exceptions. It starts empty.
14. `docs/OPERATIONS_RUNBOOK.md`, "Consumers: retry and DLQ" (l.1257-1261). The command becomes metadata-only:
    `--property print.value=false --property print.key=true --property print.headers=true --property print.partition=true --property print.offset=true --property print.timestamp=true`.
    - Add the single-record value procedure: `--partition N --offset M --max-messages 1`.
    - Add the rule: never `--from-beginning` with values; never paste output into an issue, PR, ticket or chat; never redirect it to a file.

### F. Alpha operations (recorded on the PR)

15. **Incident check before deploy.** Run a read-only count on alpha (SSM, `pos_user`): registrations per `scheme`, and vendors with any registration. **Counts only, never values.** Post the counts on the PR.
    - If any registration may belong to a real person or business, **stop and escalate to the platform owner** as a data incident (ruling 6).
    - Expected: zero, or synthetic only.
    - Also count, **counts only**, the stored registrations and the `supplier.vendor.updated` outbox payload registrations whose `scheme` or `region` breaks item 8's shapes. A non-zero count **stops the scrub** until those registrations are re-entered through the vendor form. The v2 scrub must never copy a non-conforming attribute onto the fact.
16. **Purge after deploy.** Confirm zero lag for every consumer group on `supplier.events.v1`. Then delete records up to the high-water mark on every partition of `supplier.events.v1` and `supplier.events.v1.dlq` with `kafka-delete-records.sh`. Record the offsets on the PR.

## Business rules and invariants
- No full registration number appears:
  - on Kafka, in `supplier_event_outbox`, or in any replica;
  - in any API response other than the reveal;
  - in any log line at any level, in a metric tag, in an exception message, or in an audit row.
- `last4` is never logged and never used as a metric tag.
- Every reveal is preceded, in its own transaction, by its audit row. No row means no number.
- Protection is uniform across schemes. Nothing branches on the scheme.
- `last4` is derived only in pos-supplier, only by the ruling-2 rule.
- **Test data:** tests, fixtures, examples and docs use obviously fake numbers only. Never a real or realistic-looking one.
  - Examples: `000-00-1234` (SSN shape; area 000 is never issued), `000000000RT0001` (BN shape), `FAKE1234`, `FAKE-123` (7 alphanumerics, so `last4 = null`).
  - Assertions compare against a constant and never print the number in a failure message (use `as("number absent")`, not a message that concatenates the value).

## Contracts

| Method and path | Permission | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/supplier/vendors`, `GET /{vendorId}` | `supplier:vendor:read` | `taxRegistrations[]` → `{registrationId, scheme, region, last4}` |
| `POST /v1/supplier/vendors`, `PUT /{vendorId}` | `supplier:vendor:write` | input `{registrationId?, scheme, number?, region?}`; masked response; 400 rules in item 8 |
| `POST /{vendorId}/tax-registrations/{registrationId}/reveal` | `supplier:vendor_tax_id:reveal` (new) | new; 200 / 400 `JUSTIFICATION_REQUIRED` / 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 403 / 404 / 500 `SUPPLIER_VENDOR_TAX_ID_UNREADABLE` |
| `GET /{vendorId}/tax-id-reveals` | `supplier:audit:read` | new; paged reveal audit |
| `supplier.vendor.updated` on `supplier.events.v1` | n/a | `schemaVersion` 2; `taxRegistrations[] {scheme, region, last4}` |

Error bodies use the module's existing envelope (`code`, `message`, `correlationId`, `fieldErrors`). The OpenAPI annotations on `SupplierVendorController` are updated for every row.

## Data / Flyway
- **pos-supplier, next free versions at merge** (V4 or later today), in this order:
  1. the Java backfill (item 5);
  2. the SQL outbox scrub (item 6);
  3. the reveal table (item 11), in the scrub's file or its own.
- No other module has a migration. The permission row comes from `generate-permissions.sh --sync`, plus the repeatable seed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Fact minimised.** **Given** a vendor saved with registration `{scheme: "SSN", number: "000-00-1234"}` **When** the fact is queued **Then**:
   - the outbox payload has `schemaVersion = 2` and `taxRegistrations = [{scheme: "SSN", region: null, last4: "1234"}]`;
   - the payload text does not contain `000-00-1234` or `000001234`. **[M]**: restoring `number` on the record or the publisher fails this AC.
2. **`last4` rule.**
   - `000000000RT0001` → `0001`;
   - `FAKE1234` → `1234`;
   - `FAKE-123` → `null`;
   - `--` → `null`. **[M]**: dropping the under-8 check fails this AC.
3. **Encrypted at rest.** **Given** a vendor saved with `000-00-1234` **Then**:
   - `supplier_vendor.tax_registrations::text` contains neither the number nor its separator-free form;
   - each element has `registrationId`, `last4` and `numberCiphertext`;
   - decrypting with the configured key returns the number.
4. **AAD binding.** **Given** a ciphertext copied into another vendor's registration **When** it is revealed **Then** 500 `SUPPLIER_VENDOR_TAX_ID_UNREADABLE`, with an `UNREADABLE` audit row, and no number is returned. **[M]**: removing `vendorId` from the AAD fails this AC.
5. **Key policy.**
   - No key with profiles `{}`, `{alpha}`, `{prod,dev}` or `{unknown}`: startup fails, and the message names `SUPPLIER_VENDOR_TAXID_ENC_KEY`.
   - `{dev}` or `{test}`: starts, with an ephemeral key and one WARN.
   - The exchange-audit key is never read by the vendor cipher.
6. **Backfill.** **Given** a pre-migration row with clear numbers in two tenants **When** the migrations run **Then**:
   - every element is encrypted, with an id and `last4`, and no `number` key remains in any row;
   - running the migration again changes nothing.
7. **Outbox scrub.** **Given** outbox rows of `supplier.vendor.updated` (published and unpublished, with a `last_error`) and of another supplier event type **When** the scrub runs **Then**:
   - the vendor rows have `schemaVersion = 2`, `last4` and no `number`, and `last_error IS NULL`;
   - the other type's row is byte-identical;
   - a `supplier.outbox.replay-requested` window over the scrubbed rows publishes no number.
8. **Masked reads.** A CONTROLLER's `GET /v1/supplier/vendors/{id}` and list return `{registrationId, scheme, region, last4}`; the response text contains no number. The same holds for the create, update, status and remit-to responses.
9. **Keep on update.** **Given** stored registration R **When** a PUT sends `{registrationId: R, scheme, region}` without `number` **Then**:
   - the stored ciphertext is unchanged;
   - no fact is queued when nothing else changed.

   **And when** it sends R with a different `scheme` and no `number` **Then** 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` with `fieldErrors[taxRegistrations[0].number]`, and nothing is written. **[M]**: allowing a scheme change on a kept entry fails this AC.
10. **Update refusals.**
    - An unknown `registrationId`: 400.
    - A new entry without `number`: 400.
    - A 65-character number: 400.
    - In each case the response body and the captured logs do not contain the submitted value.
11. **Reveal.** **Given** a CONTROLLER and reason `"Verifying W-9 received 2026-10-08"` **When** they reveal R **Then**:
    - 200 with the number and `Cache-Control: no-store`;
    - exactly one `supplier_vendor_tax_id_reveal` row with `outcome = REVEALED`, the actor, roles, reason and correlation id, and no number or `last4`.

    **And when** the reason is `"checking 000-00-1234 per W-9"` against stored `000-00-1234` **Then**:
    - 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`, and the body contains no number;
    - exactly one row with `outcome = REASON_REJECTED` and `reason` null.

    **[M]**: skipping the audit row on this refusal fails this AC.
12. **Reveal refusals.**
    - ACCOUNTING_CLERK, GENERAL_MANAGER and SUPPORT: 403, with no audit row.
    - Reason of 9 characters: 400 `JUSTIFICATION_REQUIRED`.
    - Unknown registration: 404.
13. **Reveal fails closed.** **Given** the audit insert fails **When** a reveal is attempted **Then** the call fails and the response contains no number. **[M]**: moving the insert after the decrypt-and-return, or into `REQUIRES_NEW`, fails this AC.
14. **Reveal audit read.** A holder of `supplier:audit:read` lists the reveals newest first. A CONTROLLER without it gets 403. Rows of another tenant are invisible (RLS).
15. **Permission.**
    - `supplier:vendor_tax_id:reveal` is in all three catalogs at the same bit, with one `CATALOG_VERSION`.
    - The seed grants it to ADMIN and CONTROLLER only.
    - `RolePermissionBaselineTest` passes, `supportIsReadOnly` included.
16. **Contract guard.**
    - `DomainEventContractTest#noRestrictedFieldNames` passes on the changed module.
    - A test-only record with a nested `List<Inner>` whose `Inner` has `taxId` makes the guard fail.
    - A test-only record with a component `supplierRegistrationNumber` makes the guard fail.

    **[M]**: removing recursion into collection element types fails this AC.
17. **No leakage in logs.** A ListAppender at DEBUG over `com.positivity.supplier` and `com.positivity.domainevents`, across create, update, reveal, replay and an outbox publish, never contains `000-00-1234`, `000001234` or `1234` in a tax-registration context. The assertion messages never print captured lines that contain the value.
18. **Runbook.** The DLQ section shows the metadata-only command and the single-record rule. No `--from-beginning` command prints values.
19. **Alpha.** The PR records:
    - the incident counts (item 15);
    - the purge offsets (item 16);
    - the `SUPPLIER_VENDOR_TAXID_ENC_KEY` provisioning, without the value.
20. **Scheme and region shapes.**
    - Refused with 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` and the matching `fieldErrors` entry:
      - `scheme: "EIN123"`;
      - a 17-character scheme `"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQ"`;
      - `region: "US-123"`.
    - The response body and the captured logs never contain the submitted value.
    - `scheme: "gst_hst"` with `region: "qc"` is accepted and stored as `GST_HST` and `QC`.
    - **[M]**: allowing a digit in `region` fails this AC.

## Tests
- **`./mvnw -pl pos-domain-events -am test`:**
  - `SupplierVendorUpdatedV1Test`: `taxRegistrationsAreCopied` is replaced by `carriesNoRegistrationNumber`, a field-name walk like `carriesNoBankDetails`;
  - round-trip with `last4`;
  - `DomainEventContractTest` with the new guard.
- **`./mvnw -pl pos-supplier -am test`:**
  - the cipher: envelope, AAD binding, key policy matrix, rotation through previous keys;
  - the `last4` rule;
  - the update matrix (item 8);
  - the reveal service (audit-first, fail-closed);
  - the controller-slice permission matrix;
  - log capture.
- **`./mvnw -pl pos-supplier -am verify`** (Testcontainers):
  - the backfill and scrub migrations on seeded pre-migration rows, across two tenants;
  - RLS on the reveal table;
  - outbox replay after the scrub.
- **`./mvnw -pl pos-security-service -am test`:** `RolePermissionBaselineTest`; the permission catalog consistency tests.
- **`./mvnw -pl pos-archunit -am -Dtest=ArchitectureTests test`.**
- **`./mvnw spotless:apply`.**
- **[M]** guards (`.claude/hooks/mutation-check-hook.sh`), listed in ACs 1, 2, 4, 9, 13 and 16. Each named mutation must make its AC fail.
- All Maven goals run on buildbox.

## Dependencies
- **BLOCKS: S24 (#2517).** S24's copy must be built against the v2 fact. The Accounting Domain amends S24 from the Security ruling on #2617.
- **Blocked by:** nothing in code. S23 (#2516) is merged.
- **Merge gate:** ADR-0044 §3 (RESTRICTED withdrawal in place) and ADR-0070 Decision 7 (registrations as `{scheme, region, last4}`) must be amended and **ACCEPTED** before this PR merges. Implementation may start now.
- **Coordinates with:**
  - S13 (#2510), for the next free permission bit (whichever merges second takes the next bit);
  - the later pos-tax scheme-vocabulary story (ruling 5).
- **Sign-offs:** Security, given in the ruling. No other sign-off is needed.
- **ADRs:**
  - platform minimum: 0011, 0013, 0014, 0017, 0018, 0024, 0026, 0027, 0062;
  - also: 0022, 0044 (R3, §3 as amended, §4), 0046, 0050 §7, 0070 (Decision 7 as amended).
- **After merge:** run **API Artifacts Sync** for the changed controllers, DTOs, events and permissions:

  ```bash
  gh workflow run api-artifacts-sync.yml --repo louisburroughs/durion-positivity-backend \
    --ref <branch> -f modules="pos-supplier pos-domain-events"
  ```

  It regenerates both specs, the permission manifests and the SDKs, and opens the PRs. Update `pos-supplier/README.md` (masked reads, reveal, key variable, update rule) in this PR.

## Frontend-visible (for S30, louisburroughs/durion-positivity-frontend#469)
- **Vendor identity:** each registration shows `scheme`, `region` and "•••• 1234". When `last4` is null, it shows "on file".
- **Edit form:**
  - a kept registration sends `registrationId` without `number`;
  - changing the scheme or region needs the number re-entered;
  - a new registration needs the number.
- **"Reveal" action:** shown only with `supplier:vendor_tax_id:reveal`. It asks for a reason (10-500 characters) and shows the number until the dialog closes. Never cached, never put in a route or query string, never logged.
- **Codes and i18n:**
  - 400 `JUSTIFICATION_REQUIRED`, `VALIDATION_ERROR` (`fieldErrors[taxRegistrations[i].number]`);
  - 404 `SUPPLIER_VENDOR_TAX_REGISTRATION_NOT_FOUND`;
  - 500 `SUPPLIER_VENDOR_TAX_ID_UNREADABLE`.

  i18n keys are needed in en, fr-CA and es.

## Decisions applied

| Source | Decision | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Security ruling #2617, 1 | All registration numbers are RESTRICTED | Number off the fact, outbox, replicas, logs |
| Security ruling #2617, 2 | `last4` CONFIDENTIAL, null under 8 | Stored and published by the owner |
| Security ruling #2617, 3 | Field-level encryption, separate key, row-bound AAD | Cipher, backfill |
| Security ruling #2617, 4 | Masked by default; `supplier:vendor_tax_id:reveal` (ADMIN, CONTROLLER); fail-closed audit; SUPPORT `vendor:read` confirmed | Reveal endpoint, audit table, seed |
| Security ruling #2617, 5 | Personal-id schemes accepted; vocabulary later | Scheme and region shape only (ADR-0072 Decision 2; Security confirmation on louisburroughs/durion#571); the closed vocabulary is #2623 |
| Security ruling #2617, 6-7 | Scrub, purge, incident check; DLQ metadata-only | Migrations, alpha steps, runbook |
| Security ruling #2617, 8 | Restricted-name guard | `DomainEventContractTest` |
| Security ruling #2617, 9 | ADR-0044 §3 / ADR-0070 D7 amendments | Merge gate |
| DECISION-INVENTORY-013 | Curated by default; raw gated and audited | Masked view; reveal |
| ADR-0044 R3 | Replicas copy the minimum | Fact carries no number |

items.title: [ARCH] [SECURITY] Vendor tax-registration numbers (possible SSN/SIN) travel in clear on SupplierVendorUpdatedV1 and its copies
items.body:
**For the Chief Architect to examine first**, then hand to the Security domain for a ruling.

## Concern

Vendor tax-registration numbers travel in clear on Kafka, and every consumer copies them unchanged.

- pos-supplier stores each vendor's tax registrations as a JSON column (`SupplierVendorEntity.taxRegistrations`, created and updated through `SupplierVendorController` `createSupplierVendor` / `updateSupplierVendor`).
- The S23 fact `SupplierVendorUpdatedV1` (pos-domain-events, `com.positivity.domainevents.supplier`) carries the full list of `TaxRegistration` values: scheme and number, verbatim (see `SupplierVendorUpdatedV1Test#taxRegistrationsAreCopied`).
- S24 (#2517) copies the fact into `ext_supplier_vendor` in pos-accounting and pos-order, verbatim.

A registration is normally a business number (EIN, GST/HST BN, VAT). For a **sole-proprietor vendor**, though, the US taxpayer id can be an **SSN** and the Canadian one a **SIN**. Once recorded, that number is:
- on the topic, for its retention period and in any replay;
- in each consumer's copy table, and their backups;
- at risk in logs, DLQs and replay tooling that print payloads.

Raised by the Accounting Domain Agent while writing #2615 (rulings comment 6061005502). #2615 itself never accepts or stores a TIN: it reads `payeeTinOnFile` / `payeeTinLast4` from S24's copy. **#2615 does not depend on the answer**, but S24's copy design does.

## Options to weigh

1. **Allow as is.** Document it as an accepted risk. Rely on topic ACLs, at-rest encryption and log redaction.
2. **Classify and restrict at entry.** pos-supplier refuses personal-id schemes (SSN, SIN, ITIN) as registrations, or stores them in a separate protected field that never goes on the fact.
3. **Minimise the fact.** The fact carries scheme, `onFile` and last 4 only. Consumers that truly need the full number (if any) read it from pos-supplier on demand, with a permission and an audit.
4. **Encrypt the field.** Field-level encryption on the fact and the copies, with key management per ADR or secret store. The cost: every consumer needs the key, and replays depend on it.

## Questions for the Chief Architect

- Which ADRs govern this? Candidates: ADR-0044 (event-only domain walls, replay and manifests), any PII/data-classification ADR, logging/redaction policy, and ADR-0071 (tax providers).
- Is there a platform-wide PII classification for event payloads? If not, does this need an ADR?
- Which consumers need the full number today (none known: #2615 needs only "on file" and last 4)?
- What is the recommended option, and what is the migration impact? S23 is merged, so the fact is live. S24 is not yet implemented, so its copy design can still change cheaply.
- Should S24 (#2517) be held or amended before it starts? S24 waits only on S13 (#2510), which is in implementation now.

## Expected output

An architecture analysis comment with a recommendation, then a hand-off to the Security domain (`agent:security`) for the ruling. If the ruling changes the S24 copy, amend #2517 before S24 is implemented.

Related: CAP:550 (louisburroughs/durion#550), S23 (supplier vendor fact), S24 #2517, #2615.

items.title: [Local K8s] CRITICAL 거래부터 AI 리포트까지 격리 배포·복구 E2E
items.body:
## 목적

전용 로컬 Kubernetes 클러스터에서 FinGuardOps의 Rule v2 합성 CRITICAL 거래부터 사건·AI 리포트 조회까지 API 중심으로 배포하고, 장애 후 복구와 소유 자원 정리를 검증한다. 이 Issue는 PR #370 병합 커밋 `c01d05ff7277e3e87c740004ec01477727d546d4`를 기준으로 한다.

## 범위

- `infra/`: 전용 namespace의 최소 Kubernetes 구성, 로컬 Backend·AI Service 이미지 빌드·고유 태그·클러스터 적재, 실행·검증·소유 자원 정리 절차. PostgreSQL 및 인증 JWT·외부 위험·Ollama 모의 fixture를 포함한다.
- 기존 `infra/local-jwt-fixture/`의 Rule v2 CRITICAL 합성 검증을 재사용하고 필요한 E2E 검증 코드만 조정한다.
- `docs/09-deployment/`: 선행 조건, 실행·장애·복구·보존 결정과 실패 시 진단을 다루는 runbook.
- 공개 API, DB schema, Rule scoring 및 업무 상태 계약은 변경하지 않는다.

## 완료 조건

1. 시작 전 전용 클러스터/namespace, 이미지, PVC/PV, Secret의 소유권과 CPU·메모리·디스크 여유를 기록한다. 기존 중지된 `minikube`, 다른 프로젝트 컨테이너, Compose 보존 volume은 소유권이 확인되지 않아 사용·정리하지 않는다. 전용 클러스터를 안전하게 확보할 수 없거나 자원이 부족하면 기동하지 않고 차단 원인을 보고한다.
2. Backend·AI Service 이미지를 로컬에서 고유 태그로 빌드해 전용 클러스터에 적재하고 외부 registry pull 없이 기동한다. Secret은 Git 밖에서 전달하고 접근 경로는 loopback으로 제한한다.
3. 전용 PostgreSQL에서 Flyway migration과 v1→v2 Rule 발행·활성 시각을 확인한다. 인증된 합성 거래의 채택 Evidence 4개·85/CRITICAL·HELD, 같은 사건 ID의 조사·Audit 및 AI 요청·execution·저장 리포트를 API와 DB에서 대조한다. 모의 Provider 결과는 실제 Qwen 성공으로 표기하지 않는다.
4. 잘못된 Secret/JWT, DB 미준비, AI Service 불통, 잘못된 이미지 참조, 중복·멱등 거래를 검사한다. readiness 실패의 트래픽 차단, Backend·AI Service 재시작 뒤 업무 상태 불변, PostgreSQL 재시작 뒤 데이터 유지, 실패 이미지에서 이전 이미지로 복귀를 검증한다. 이미지 복귀가 적용된 migration이나 발행된 Rule을 되돌린다고 주장하지 않는다.
5. 정리 전에 DB 증거 및 PVC/PV 보존 필요성을 판단한다. namespace 삭제가 저장소를 함께 삭제하는지 먼저 확인하고, 판단 전에는 namespace 전체 삭제·volume 삭제를 실행하지 않는다. 종료 뒤 이번 실행이 소유한 정확한 자원과 다른 프로젝트 재고를 대조한다.

## 범위 밖과 검증 경계

Frontend·실제 Keycloak Browser Gate, Kafka consumer·lag, 전체 관측 스택, 실제 Qwen 반복 평가, GHCR 잠금 해제, AWS 유료 배포, outbox 보존·경고 정책, CRITICAL 오탐률 평가는 이 Issue의 완료 조건이 아니다. 각 기존 Compose 프로젝트의 검증 결과를 이번 Kubernetes E2E 성공으로 합산하지 않는다. AI Provider 호출량·토큰·비용의 미측정값을 0으로 기록하지 않는다.

## 사전점검 근거

원격 `main`에 Kubernetes manifest/Helm/Kustomize/배포 스크립트가 없고 Frontend 서비스 배포 이미지 절차도 없다. 점검 시 Windows `kubectl`에는 context가 없으며 `minikube`·`kind`·`helm` 명령을 확인하지 못했다. 중지된 minikube Docker 자원의 FinGuardOps 소유권은 입증되지 않았고 가용 RAM은 순간 관측 약 2.2 GiB였다. 따라서 배포 성공은 미검증이며, 구현·실행 전 전용 클러스터 방식·자원 할당·PVC/PV 보존 정책을 확인해야 한다.

items.title: cli: show consumer group lag, and delete or reset consumer offsets

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: A change that improves our (or users) QoL

items.body:
## Problem

- You cannot see consumer lag (the messages that a group did not consume yet). `consumer-group get` shows members and partitions, but no offsets. `consumer-offset get` shows one partition per call.
- The CLI cannot delete a consumer offset. The SDK (`core/common/src/traits/consumer_offset_client.rs:65`) and the binary protocol (code 122) support it. The HTTP API deletes only regular consumer offsets (`core/server/src/http/handlers.rs:1530`).
- The CLI cannot set a consumer group offset. Over TCP, QUIC and WebSocket, `consumer-offset set -k consumer-group` fails with error 5009, because the CLI is not a member of the group (`core/server/src/namespace.rs:280`):

  ```
  Consumer group member with client ID: 0 does not own partition: 0 at the current generation (rebalance in progress).
  ```

  No rebalance runs, because the group has no members. Binary errors carry only the code, so the client fills the fields with zeros (#3735). Over HTTP, the same command writes a regular consumer offset instead (#4408). `-k external-group` works, but Iggy consumer groups never read external group offsets (#4392).

## Proposal

- Add a partitions table to `consumer-group get`: partition, member, current offset, stored offset and lag. A client does not need to be a member to read a group offset. The stored offset is the last consumed offset, so the lag is the current offset minus the stored offset. If no offset is stored, the lag is the message count of the partition.
- Add `consumer-offset delete`, with the same arguments as `consumer-offset get`.
- Server: if the group has no members, accept an offset write or delete for it from a non-member. If the group has members, keep the current fence. The Kafka admin API has the same rule: it resets the offsets of an empty group only.
- Add `consumer-group reset <STREAM_ID> <TOPIC_ID> <GROUP_ID>` with `--to-earliest`, `--to-latest`, `--to-offset <N>` or `--to-timestamp <TIME>`. Print the plan first, and write it only with `--execute`.
- `--to-offset N` stores `N - 1`, because the next poll starts after the stored offset. `--to-earliest` and `--to-offset 0` delete the offset.

## Notes

- Agree on the server rule before coding. The lag view does not depend on it. Until the rule exists, `consumer-offset delete` works only for regular consumers and external groups.
- The membership check and the offset write are not atomic, so a consumer that joins during a reset can overwrite it. Before a reset, stop all consumers of the group and wait for `consumer_group.session_timeout`.
- An offset write needs only the poll permission. With the new rule, any user who can poll the topic can reset an idle group.
- A stored group offset holds back retention. If a reset deletes it, retention can remove messages that the group did not read. The help text must say this.
- Over HTTP, the group kind is lost (#4408), so the lag view needs TCP, QUIC or WebSocket until #4279 is done. Offset reads come from the local replica, so the lag can be stale (#4409).
